answer: Each agent must lock a scarce, nontransferable credential issued after a human or trusted-device check, then post a bond before it can earn reputation or claim rewards. A public beacon records the credential’s use, while a lantern flags simultaneous claims from the same credential; an anchor keeps the bond locked through disputes. Creating many identities therefore requires passing many checks and tying up real capital, which can be slashed when credentials are duplicated or claims are fraudulent.
